scope: Source-linked development observations, not human ratings or an estimate of question accuracy. All nine classroom cases were inspected.

cases.observation: Place, discussion leader and reading material are supported. The leader question has awkward grammatical agreement. Targets are whole statements, broader than the minimal answers to where/who/what questions.
The road-repair cause is appropriate, but the question substitutes the unrelated word 'استغراب' for the journey taking time. The driver item is supported with a broader-than-needed statement target.

Germination count and watering duration are supported. The planting question repeats 'ما هو ما' awkwardly and asks a broad action question. All three statement targets exceed the shortest sufficient answers.

Place, reading material and recorded suggestions are supported. The record item has a focused answer; the other two use whole statements. The passage offers limited conceptual material, so these are relevant recall questions rather than evidence of deep understanding.
The journey-duration why-question uses the stated road-repair reason. The destination question is supported, although its statement target includes the driver and action as well as the museum.
Germination count, watering duration and planting action are source-supported. Statement targets are broader than minimal answers. The planting item is less focused than the count/duration items.
Meeting place, Salma's role and reading material are supported and readable. Statement targets are broad but contain the requested facts.
Departure time and driver are supported. The duration-and-cause item is a two-part question, matching a two-fact statement target but less focused than one question per fact.

Count and duration questions are clear and supported. The planting item asks for the situation, testing a relatively incidental classroom setting rather than the experimental action. It also copies much of its long target into the question; whole-answer leakage checks do not detect partial-answer copying.
